# Public scalar records imported into pure notebooks

**Goal.** Admit the public immutable scalar-record package APIs implemented in Wave 25 into the existing pure notebook execution profile, preserving nominal identity and reliable invalidation.

**Exclusive ownership.** All five `crates/cgx2-notebook-*` crates, examples, tests and owned evidence. Do not edit syntax, sema, package, CLI, emitters, runtime, verifier, foreign, bench, root Cargo files or shared documents. Use the frozen public checked-package/import metadata and `Value::Record` APIs. Report an indispensable missing accessor as a concrete blocker.

## Contract

1. Admit explicit direct imports from the existing pinned local acyclic package profile when the relevant public record has one to eight immutable `i64`/`Bool` fields and imported functions are pure in the previously supported call profile. Support qualified constructors, passing/returning imported records, field projection, and local pure notebook functions whose annotations use the imported public record. Preserve declaration-order fields, source-order argument evaluation, checked arithmetic and the existing conditional function semantics. Do not broaden transitive call/import support, add private-record access, reexports, mutable/nested/generic/managed/foreign records, effects or contracts.
2. Use defining-module plus record name as nominal identity throughout lowering, retained bindings, function signatures, display/protocol validation and replay. Same-named/same-shaped records from two modules and a local record remain distinct. Never flatten a value to its short name or structural fields for type checks. Keep qualified source annotation/constructor lookup dependent on explicit imports and the package's visibility checks. Reject ambiguous local/module roots and private metadata before executing a worker or replaying an earlier cell.
3. Extend existing bounded tagged worker serialization and retained-value validation to represent qualified imported identities without relaxing size/field/type checks. Accept only identities backed by the checked import environment. Preserve exact i64/Bool values, Unicode module/record/field names, existing version compatibility behavior, maximum frame/replay/value limits and failure handling. A stale/mismatched imported definition must not deserialize into a different nominal type. Keep local-record notebooks backward compatible.
4. Track dependency edges from imports, annotations, constructors, field uses and imported/local function bodies, including inactive conditional branches and annotation-only uses. Bind provenance to the defining module's source/hash and relevant package inputs. Editing/deleting/replacing a module record, changing its visibility/fields, changing the manifest/import declaration or switching package roots must invalidate dependent cells and cached retained values while independent cells keep valid outputs. Recheck module hashes/canonical paths at the existing package boundary; do not silently reuse stale package metadata.
5. Publish definitions/bindings/outputs only after complete success. Errors, cancellation, timeout, protocol failures, wrong nominal values and stale imports preserve prior valid state and never replay effectful cells. Preserve step/depth limits and replay admission. Save/reopen, selected-cell rerun, affected rerun, Restart and Run All, clean sweep and export must have the same supported-profile behavior. Imported module source remains governed by existing package asset rules; do not make an exported notebook claim to be self-contained if required package inputs were not embedded.
6. Add a readable `.cgnb` example with its small local package fixture and exercise CLI and loopback UI. Diagnostics name the cell and relevant CGx2 source span. Document exactly which imports work and which remain rejected; no performance or foreign-memory claim follows.

## Verification and handoff

Test two modules with identical record/field names, local-versus-imported identities, reordered constructor fields, annotation-only dependencies, private/unknown/missing imports, Unicode and generated-name collisions, module edit/delete/visibility changes, package-root changes, selective invalidation, worker tampering/wrong identity, failure recovery, save/reopen/restart/clean sweep/export behavior and independent-cell preservation. Include inactive-branch dependencies and no hidden effect replay. Run all five notebook suites offline, HTTP tests where permitted, formatting and owned Clippy `-D warnings`. Use existing package regression fixtures read-only where useful. Commit owned files/evidence, record knowledge, report commands/results/resource bounds/unsupported cases and commit, then stop.
